s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: 10-day history of fever
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
past medical history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
white blood cell count: 2.3 × 103/μL
hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL
platelet count: 29 × 103/μL
C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL
blood culture: negative
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, tender skin lesions, and inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, consistent with Sweet syndrome

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions with violaceous and crusted centers, and history of immunocompromise

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: inflammatory infiltrate and nuclear dust on biopsy, although no obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Multiple Myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: past medical history and recent chemotherapy, with possible skin involvement

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: immunohistochemistry positive for myeloperoxidase, and history of multiple myeloma with possible transformation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers, along with the laboratory findings of elevated C-reactive protein and negative blood culture, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The skin biopsy findings of inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can present with similar skin lesions, the absence of ulceration and the specific histopathological features make it less likely.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The skin biopsy did not show obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Multiple Myeloma
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of multiple myeloma, the current presentation is not typical for a myeloma-related complication.

rejected.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of acute myeloid leukemia in the provided information, and the patient's recent chemotherapy for multiple myeloma makes this diagnosis less likely at this time.
